key: And Joseph said unto them: ‘Fear not; for am I in the place of God?
s: After Jacob’s burial, the brothers, fearing Joseph’s revenge, send word of their father’s last charge and fall before him as bondmen; Rashi, on 50:19, reads his answer as asking how he alone could harm those whose evil design God had already turned to good.

evidence.words: שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹמוֹ אֲנִי? בִּתְמִיהָ, אִם הָיִיתִי רוֹצֶה לְהָרַע לָכֶם, כְּלוּם אֲנִי יָכוֹל? וַהֲלֹא אַתֶּם כֻּלְּכֶם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטוֹבָה וְהֵיאַךְ אֲנִי לְבַדִּי יָכוֹל לְהָרַע לָכֶם
evidence.gloss: Am I perhaps in His place? (said in wonder). If I wished to harm you, could I at all? Did not all of you design evil against me, and the Holy One, blessed be He, designed it for good; how then can I alone harm you?

reason: verse.js ok (Genesis 50:19, at [49,19], 15 words). Plain sense matches 50:15 to 18 (brothers fear requital, send the message of their father’s command, fall before him saying they are bondmen). Rashi on 50:19 reads the question as: could I harm you at all, when all of you designed evil and God designed it for good; how can I alone harm you. The sentence paraphrases this without drift (Rashi’s 50:21 comment gives further reasons, not contradicted). entry-check ok, 44 words.
